full_judgment:
3. Admittedly accused-petitioner is the Managing Director and complainant is the Director of M/s. Master Industries Limited and co-accused Saidul Islam Khan (Tutul) is the Accountant of M/s. Rahim Metal Industries Limited purchased by the said Master Industries Limited from the Government. 

 4. In complaint Case No. 761a1 of 1984 which gave rise to Special Case No. 60 of 1986 complainant opposite party alleged that for purchasing Rahim Metal Industries from the Government Master Industries Limited had to pay $46,816.93 purchased in auction on 11.5.78. On that date auction rate per pound was Taka 35.60 but the accused persons showed expenditure of Taka 19,17,153.20 paisa in the account of the M/s Master Industries Limited instead of Taka 16,66,682.70 showing purchase of pound @ Taka 40.95 and thus misappropriated the sum of Taka 2,50,470.50 paisa by falsification of accounts. 

 8. Mr. Md. Abdul Malek, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in these Rules, contended that the dispute is between the majority and minority share holders of M/s. Master Industries Limited and the complainant having a minority share holding failed to become the Managing Director and therefore filed the 4 criminal cases against the Managing Director petitioner representing the majority shares of the Company with maliciously false allegations to unnecessarily harass him by abusing the process of the Court. He further contended that after the balance-sheet is prepared and audited by a Chartered Accountant and approved by the share-holders of the Company the same is conclusive and cannot be questioned and, as such, criminal prosecution cannot lie in respect of past transactions of the company which formed part of the audited balance sheet approved by the share holders of the Company. He further submitted that Managing Director of a private limited Company in which Government has no share is not a public servant and, as such, Special Judge has no jurisdiction to try the alleged offence of criminal breach of trust. So proceedings of Special Case Nos. 60-62 of 1986 pending in the Court of the Special Judge, Dhaka are liable to be quashed, In respect of proceedings of petition Case No. 828a1/1991 pending in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, his contention is that the allegations of misappropriation by showing less amount in the books of accounts are fantastic and made only for the purpose of harassing the petitioner by abusing the process of the Court. So the proceedings of that case should also be quashed. 

 10. Section 409 of the Penal Code provides for punishment for criminal breach of trust by a public servant or a banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent. Unless one of the accused persons is a public servant under the provisions of Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 and the offence alleged is an offence under the said Act, Senior Special Judge has no jurisdiction to take cognizance of an offence under section 409 of the Penal Code. So we have to consider whether the petitioner is a public servant either within the meaning of section 21 of the Penal Code or section 2(b) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 (a) in the service or pay of the Government or remunerated by the Government by fees or commission for the performance of any public duty 

 (b) in the service or pay of a local authority or of a corporation, body or authority established by or under any law or of a firm or company in which any part of the interest or share capital is held by, or vested in, the Government." 

 It is nobody's case that any part of the interest or share or share capital of M/s. Master Industries Limited is held by or vested in the Government. So the petitioner is not a "public servant" within the meaning of section 21 of the Penal Code. 

 12. Section 2(b) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 as amended by section 3 of the Criminal Law Amendment (Amendment) Ordinance 1978 (Ordinance VI of 1978) defines a "public servant" as follows: 

 14. From the above it is clear that a "body corporate" is an artificial person or legal entity having separate and distinct personality from that of the private individual or individuals constituting the same by or under any law. When a body corporate is constituted and established by a particular law then such a body corporate is known as a "statutory corporation" as the incorporation is made by law and not by individuals. When private individuals form an association or a body and register the same under the provisions of law to give such association or body a separate and distinct artificial personality or legal entity then the same also becomes a corporation or a company. Instances of statutory corporation" are the Bangladesh Jute Corporation, established by the Bangladesh Jute Corporation Ordinance 1973 and Jiban Bima Corporation and Sadharan Bima Corporation established by the Insurance Corporation Ordinance, 1973. Corporations other than the statutory Corporations are those associations or bodies constituted by private individuals and incorporated or registered under the provisions of Companies Act or any other law. So, body Corporate includes both statutory Corporation and other corporation or company private or public. But in the above provision of section 2(b) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act "body Corporate" has been used to mean corporation other than "Statutory Corporation". So Master Industries Limited is a body corporate as mentioned in the aforesaid provision of section 2(b) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958. Therefore, we are of the view that the petitioner as Managing Director of Master Industries Limited is a "public servant" within the meaning of section 2(b) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 as a Director of a 'Body Corporate' as mentioned in the said provisions. So we find no illegality in registering the 3 complaint cases as Special Case Nos. 60-62 of 1986 in the Court of the Special Judge, Dhaka after receipt of records of the said complaint cases by the Senior Special Judge, Dhaka from the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka.
